thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High p99 latency observed on /v1/stream (3m window) — p99=7.2s, p95=0.5s. SLO p99=1s. Affected region: us-west-3. Routing heatmap shows a concentration on node gpu-az3-n12. https://dash.re/redwood/incidents/1719456789 :rotating_light:

devon.ng: Oncall ack, investigating. Is this causing customer-visible errors or just slow tails?

sana.jain: Confirming customer impact — some streaming requests are timing out at the client side. p95 still ok-ish but p99 tail shows repeated stalls where token streaming pauses for 10-20s then resumes. Traces point to long waits at the model inference step (gpu device).

rafael: Infra telemetry: gpu-az3-n12 shows rising correctable ECC counts over last 20m, GPU temp ~85C, fans at 97-99%. NVML logs have multiple "correctable ECC error" entries and driver shows retries. Can paste logs if needed.

devon.ng: Ops — can we isolate that node and route traffic away? Want to avoid wider cascade.

ops-bot: Suggested mitigation steps:

```
# cordon node
kubectl cordon node/gpu-az3-n12
# gracefully drain pods with timeout
kubectl drain node/gpu-az3-n12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# update routing policy to remove node from inference pool
redwoodctl pool update --region us-west-3 --remove-node gpu-az3-n12
```

lee-barton: I'll take the drain. Starting cordon now. Will also lower max_concurrency for the pool to reduce pressure while we evacuate.

lee-barton: cordon complete. Eviction in progress, about 18/24 inference pods drained. Redirecting new traffic off that rack via routing override.

anita: Customer impact summary (live): three tenants reporting timeouts (one enterprise support case open). Percentage of affected streamed requests ~0.9% of overall platform traffic but concentrated to a few large customers in us-west-3. SLAs: two have 99.9% availability clauses; we may have p99 SLO breach window here. Collecting support logs.

devon.ng: Good. Rafael — can you confirm whether ECC is correctable-only or if we're seeing uncorrectable events? Also check for NVLink/PCIe errors.

rafael: So far only correctable ECC; no UCEs (uncorrectable) in kernel logs. However the corrected rate is spiking which correlates with increased latency due to internal retries and recovery. I'm also seeing occasional GPU driver stalls and a couple of kernel messages about UVM timeouts. I'll keep node offline until HW shop swaps the card.

sana.jain: Early mitigation: we've enabled model-fallback for the affected route to use a smaller quantized variant (q4) and reduced streaming chunk size to reduce per-token latency. Degraded quality for some requests but reduces stall probability. Implemented at 1719456902.

devon.ng: Nice. After drain completes, what's p99?

rafael: Post-redirect numbers: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 2.4s (improved from 7.2s). Still above SLO but trending down. Streaming stalls appear much less frequent.

lee-barton: Drain finished, node marked unschedulable and isolated. I've left it powered on in case we need deeper live debugging, but it's out of rotation. Opening a ticket with hwops to replace GPU on aws host id i-0a12b3c4.

anita: Notifying impacted customers via status page and support ticketing. Draft message ready: "We're investigating elevated latency on streaming in us-west-3; we've rerouted traffic and applied mitigations; follow-up postmortem will be shared."

devon.ng: Good. For postmortem we should capture: anomaly start time, metrics (p95/p99 pre/post), ECC counts/time-series, node logs, routing decisions, mitigation timeline, and customer impact. Assigning PM for postmortem: @anita.

rafael: I'll attach NVML dumps, driver logs, and corrected ECC histogram to the incident ticket. Also recommending we add an alert for corrected ECC rate rising above X/min for autosuppression to prevent single-node tail events.

sana.jain: Also recommend we add a streaming-tail synthetic test that exercises long-horizon KV cache to catch stalls earlier. Filed RFC PR: https://git.re/redwood/engops/streaming-synthetics/pull/42

devon.ng: Handing off monitoring and follow-ups to @lee-barton for the rest of shift. If p99 creeps above 3s again, please escalate to infra oncall.

lee-barton: Taking it. I'll run 30m watch and validate eviction metrics. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT: ticket created INC-2026-1284. Postmortem owner: anita. Current state: mitigated (node isolated, traffic rerouted, fallback enabled).
